`pwdResetRequired` is declared as a nullable `Integer` flag. Any consumer doing `if (resp.getPwdResetRequired())` or comparing with `== 1` can hit an NPE / unboxing failure when the field is not populated (e.g. deserialized legacy payloads or code paths that forget to set it). Both branches read the raw `user.getDataScope()`, which is not guaranteed non-null: `SecurityUser` is rebuilt from the cached `PermissionContext` (`rebuildFromContext` / `ctx.getDataScope()`), so a null scope is possible. Note the controller already guards the endpoint with `@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")`, so this path is only reachable for non-`SecurityUser` principals.

content: Recursion has no cycle/depth guard. A row whose `parent_id` points to itself (or any parent/child cycle) makes `buildMenuTree(menus, m.getId())` return the node itself again, producing infinite recursion and a `StackOverflowError` (unrecoverable request failure). Since this method already accounts for hand-written/anomalous `sys_menu` rows (see `dedupeByPath`), add a visited-id set (or a depth cap) to make the traversal cycle-safe.

N+1 query pattern: one `deptMapper.selectById` per position (and the same org id may repeat across positions). This runs on every login, so collect the distinct `orgId`s first and load them with a single `selectBatchIds` call.

Clearing the IP-wide failure counter on any successful login defeats the intent of `MAX_IP_LOGIN_FAILS` (anti distributed brute force): an attacker holding one valid credential can log in once to reset `login_fail_ip:<ip>` and immediately get another 20 failed attempts against other accounts, indefinitely. Only the per-user key should be cleared on success; the IP-level counter should be left to expire on its own (or be decremented rather than deleted).

content: `increment` creates the key without a TTL and `expire` is a second, non-atomic round trip. If the JVM dies / the `expire` call fails between the two commands, `pwd_reset_ip:<ip>` is left without expiry, which permanently returns 429 for that IP. Use a single atomic operation (Lua script or `opsForValue().set(...)` on creation with TTL) so the counter can never become immortal.

Check-then-act race: the key is only written after the SMS has been sent (`set(rateKey, "1", ...)` further down), so concurrent requests for the same username all pass `hasKey` and each sends a real SMS. Make the reservation atomic with the check, e.g. `Boolean ok = redisTemplate.opsForValue().setIfAbsent(rateKey, "1", Duration.ofSeconds(RATE_LIMIT_SECONDS)); if (!Boolean.TRUE.equals(ok)) throw ...` (and delete the key if sending fails so the user can retry).

content: `size` is taken from the request without any lower-bound validation. The service only clamps the upper bound (`Math.min(size, MAX_PAGE_SIZE)`), so a request such as `?size=-1` (or `0`) is passed straight into `new Page<>(current, size)` and ends up as a negative/zero `LIMIT` in the generated SQL, which either throws a SQL syntax error (HTTP 500) or returns nothing unexpectedly. Please reject/clamp values below 1 on the entry point (e.g. `@Min(1)` with `@Validated`, or `Math.max(1, ...)` when building the page).

Consider clamping the values before delegating (e.g. `int safeCurrent = Math.max(current, 1); int safeSize = Math.min(Math.max(size, 1), 200);`) or adding `@Validated` + `@Min/@Max` on the parameters.

Because `SysDictService.deleteType` only blocks deletion when `builtIn == 1`, a client can first PUT `{"builtIn":0}` to this endpoint (or POST it in `createType`/`createData`) and then DELETE the type, bypassing the "系统内置字典不允许删除" protection. `dictCode`/`status`/`createdAt` can likewise be tampered with. content: No input validation on the write endpoints: the bodies are accepted without `@Valid`/`@Validated` and neither `SysDictType` nor `SysDictData` declares Bean Validation constraints, so null/blank `dictCode`, `dictName`, `dictValue`, etc. can be persisted (e.g. a null `dictCode` makes the duplicate check in `SysDictService.createType` pass and inserts an unusable dictionary entry). Suggest annotating the parameters with `@Valid` and adding constraints such as `@NotBlank`/`@Size` on the entity (or a request DTO), plus matching `@Validated` handling.

`create` binds the request body directly to the `SysGroup` entity without validation and, unlike `update` (which forces `group.setId(id)`), it never clears the client-supplied `id`. With MyBatis-Plus `IdType.AUTO`, a non-null `id` in the body is inserted as-is, and fields such as `status` can also be set arbitrarily by the caller (mass assignment). Consider clearing `id`/`status` server-side or introducing a dedicated request DTO annotated with `@Valid` for required fields (`groupName`, `groupCode`).

content: The broad `catch (Exception e)` silently swallows all failures and returns a transparent SVG without any logging. Real failures (e.g. config lookup errors, malformed logo URL, file system problems) become invisible and are very hard to diagnose in production. Add at least a warn-level log before degrading.

N+1 query: `positionService.getRules(id)` performs a DB query (`ruleMapper.selectByPositionId`) for every element of `positionIds`, so a request assigning N positions triggers up to N queries. Use a single batch query (e.g. add `SysPositionService.hasAnyRules(Collection<Long> positionIds)` doing one `selectCount(... in(positionIds))` or a `selectByPositionIds` + in-memory check) and evaluate the result once.

Check-then-act (TOCTOU) race: the permission check and the assignment are not atomic. A concurrent request to `PUT /{positionId}/rules` (or any other path that binds rules to the position) can attach permission rules to the position in the window between this check and `assignUserPositions`, letting a non-admin obtain a rule-carrying position and bypass the intended protection. Perform the check inside the same transaction as the assignment (or serialize on the position row, e.g. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` / re-validate after assignment with rollback on violation).

content: The rule-binding endpoint lacks the admin guard that `assignUserPositions` enforces for "positions carrying permission rules are privileged". A user holding only `system:position:edit` can call this endpoint on a position that is (or later becomes) assigned to them – or on another user's position – and attach arbitrary permission rules, granting those permissions at login. Note `saveRules` also performs no group-scope check on `positionId`, so cross-group positions can be modified. Restrict rule binding to admins, or validate that the submitted rule IDs are a subset of the caller's own effective permissions.

`body.get("ruleIds")` returns null when the key is absent or explicitly null, and `SysPositionService.saveRules(positionId, null)` deletes all existing bindings and returns. So a malformed/partial request silently wipes the position's permission rules instead of failing. Reject a missing key explicitly (same concern applies to `positionIds` in `assignUserPositions`), e.g. use a typed DTO with `@NotNull`, or throw `BusinessException` when the list is null.

content: Read endpoint lacks the assignee-type whitelist enforced by its PUT counterpart (`updateAssigneeScopes`). Here `type` is passed straight to `rolePermScopeService.getAssigneeScopes(type, key)` → `WHERE assignee_type=? AND assignee_key=?`, so any unsupported/typo value (e.g. `ROLE`, `POSITON`) silently returns an empty list instead of a clear error, which is hard to diagnose from the UI. Note the javadoc above also claims this is "岗位级(assigneeType=POSITION)" while the endpoint actually accepts `USER` (and, unvalidated, anything else). Suggest reusing the same `ScopeConfig.ASSIGNEE_POSITION/USER` check (or a shared validation helper used by both PUT and GET) and fixing the javadoc.

The request body is bound directly to the persistence entity and is never validated (`@Valid` would be a no-op here since `SysPermissionRule` declares no constraints). Consequences: (1) clients can over-post server-managed fields such as `id`/`createTime`/`updateTime` — `createTime` is only auto-filled when null, so a caller-supplied value is persisted; (2) arbitrary `ruleType`/`operator`/`targetColumn` strings are persisted verbatim and later consumed by `PermissionRuleEngine`, where an unrecognized `operator` matches no `switch` branch and therefore emits no WHERE clause — i.e. a mis-typed rule silently disables the data-permission filter instead of failing. Recommend accepting a dedicated DTO (or ignoring server-managed fields) and whitelist-validating `ruleType`/`operator` before delegating to the service. The same applies to `update(...)` below.

content: `Map.get` returns null when a key is missing, and `@RequestBody` can also bind a JSON literal `null` (making `params` itself null). Both values are passed straight to `SysUserService.changePassword`, which calls `passwordEncoder.matches(oldPassword, ...)` / `passwordEncoder.encode(newPassword)` — Spring Security's encoders throw `IllegalArgumentException` on a null password, turning a malformed request into an HTTP 500 instead of a 400. Validate the presence of both parameters (and `params` itself) before delegating.

The org-admin guard only validates the *current* state of the target user (`canManageUser(id)`); the mutated fields in the request body are never scope-checked. `SysUserService.update` copies `deptId`/`officeId`/`status` verbatim from the body, so an org admin who manages this user can relocate them into a department of another organization (or flip their status) — the target org of the *write* is not validated, unlike `create` which validates the target org. Add a scope check on the new organization/department (e.g. resolve the department's org and verify `canManageOrg`) before delegating.

content:
The auto-fill field names here do not match the global MetaObjectHandler, which only fills properties named `createdAt` and `updatedAt` (see MybatisPlusConfig#metaObjectHandler: strictInsertFill("createdAt") / strictInsertFill("updatedAt") / strictUpdateFill("updatedAt")). Because these properties are named `createTime`/`updateTime`, the fill handler can never set them.

Since fields annotated with `FieldFill.INSERT/INSERT_UPDATE` are included in the generated INSERT/UPDATE SQL unconditionally, they will be written as NULL, overriding the column defaults (`create_time DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `update_time ... ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`), so the audit timestamps end up empty. This is also inconsistent with the rest of the module (SysUser/SysGroup/SysRole/BizCustomer all use `createdAt`/`updatedAt`).

Fix by aligning with the handler (explicit column mapping keeps the existing DB columns), or alternatively extend MetaObjectHandler to also fill `createTime`/`updateTime`.

`createdAt`/`updatedAt` are missing the `@TableField(fill = ...)` annotations that sibling entities use (see `SysUser.createdAt/updatedAt`, `SysPosition.createTime/updateTime`). The global `MetaObjectHandler` in `MybatisPlusConfig` uses `strictInsertFill`/`strictUpdateFill`, which only populate fields declared with a fill strategy, so for `SysRole` these columns are never filled by the handler — the code silently depends on the DB defaults (`DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`). Consequences: (1) the in-memory entity returned right after `roleMapper.insert(role)` keeps `createdAt`/`updatedAt == null`; (2) because `SysRole` is also bound directly from the request body in `SysRoleController` (`@RequestBody SysRole role`), a client-supplied `createdAt`/`updatedAt` value is non-null and therefore written verbatim into the column, bypassing the intended generation logic. Adding the fill annotations keeps the entity consistent with the rest of the project and closes the naive timestamp injection path.

    private LocalDateTime updatedAt;

content: The Javadoc states this mapper is append-only (only insert/select), but extending `BaseMapper<SysAuditLog>` still publishes `updateById`/`update`/`deleteById`/`delete` to every caller. Those calls compile fine and only blow up at runtime with a DB trigger error, so the append-only guarantee is enforced late and non-obviously. Consider narrowing the contract at compile time, e.g. declaring an explicit mapper that exposes only the needed statements (`insert` + `selectPage`/`selectList`), or add a comment/`@Deprecated` note on the inherited mutation methods so callers know they are unsupported.

The Javadoc states this mapper is "append-only (仅 insert/select)", but extending `BaseMapper<SysRuleVersion>` also exposes `updateById`/`update`/`deleteById`/`delete` etc. Nothing prevents the service/controller layer from calling them, so the append-only invariant of a rule-audit table is not actually enforced. Consider not extending `BaseMapper` (declare only `insert`/`selectPage`/`selectList`), or marking this as read-only and overriding the mutation methods to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`.

`createdAt` 未声明 MyBatis-Plus 的自动填充注解。项目在 `MybatisPlusConfig#metaObjectHandler()` 中通过 `strictInsertFill(..., "createdAt", ...)` 统一填充创建时间，而 `strictInsertFill` 只会对声明了 `@TableField(fill = FieldFill.INSERT)` 的字段生效（参见 `BaseEntity`、`SysUser`、`SysGroup` 等实体）。当前该字段没有任何 fill 声明，实体被 `SysConfigService#recordRuleVersion` 插入时 `createdAt` 为 null；只是因为迁移脚本 `V2026.09.19.5__rule_version.sql` 中 `created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` 才没有报错，一旦表结构默认值被调整（或改用其它数据源/建表脚本）该插入会直接失败。建议与项目其它实体保持一致，补上 `@TableField(fill = FieldFill.INSERT)`。

content: Inconsistent parameter binding: sibling mappers in the same package (SysPermissionRuleMapper#selectByUserId, SysRoleOrgMapper#selectByUserId, SysUserOrgMapper#selectByUserId) all bind the userId with `@Param("userId")`. Here the annotation is missing. It happens to work only because the method has a single simple (non-collection) parameter, which MyBatis resolves by value; as soon as a second parameter is added, or `useActualParamName`/`-parameters` behaviour changes, `#{userId}` will no longer resolve and the query fails at runtime. Please declare it explicitly for robustness and consistency.

The query has no deterministic ordering, yet its result is surfaced directly as the `positions` list of the login/user-info response (AuthService#getUserInfo) and the entity exposes a `sort` column (see sys_position DDL) meant for exactly this purpose. content: Recursion has no cycle/self-reference guard: if the seeded data ever contains a self-parent or a parent cycle (e.g. a menu whose `parent_id` points to itself or forms a loop), `buildTree(list, m.getId())` recurses forever until StackOverflowError. `buildTree` rescans the whole `list` on every recursive call, so building the tree is O(n²) (each of the n nodes triggers a full-list filter pass). `Stream.peek` is documented as being for debugging only and is not guaranteed to run for every element in all stream pipelines; using it here to mutate entities (`setChildren`) makes the side effect implicit and skips the returned list's intended `map`/`collect` semantics. So the map is effectively a hardcoded 2-branch switch, and if anyone adds a third mapping (e.g. "customer_type" -> "customer_type"), `updateData` will silently overwrite the wrong customer column (`dev_type`) instead of the intended one. The ternary is also duplicated for `.eq` and `.set`. Consider mapping the dict code directly to the target `SFunction`/column and using it once, e.g.:

```java
private static final Map<String, SFunction<BizCustomer, ?>> DICT_COLUMN_MAP = Map.of(
        "industry", BizCustomer::getIndustry,
        "dev_type", BizCustomer::getDevType);
```

and then apply it via `.eq(column, oldValue).set(column, newValue)`.

`updateData` goes to the trouble of propagating a changed `dictValue` to `biz_customer`, but `deleteData` silently removes the dictionary item and leaves all customer rows still holding the now-orphaned value. With dirty data of the kind this method explicitly tries to defend against (a self-referencing node, or a parent chain that forms a cycle such as A→B→A), `byId.containsKey(cur)` stays true forever and this becomes an infinite loop that pins the request thread. With a full org tree this means one query per department (and the same leader is re-queried when it leads several departments). Classic check-then-act race: the child/user counts are read in two independent statements and `deleteById` runs afterwards without any transaction or lock. A concurrent request creating a child department or assigning a user to this department between the check and the delete silently produces an orphan node / user pointing at a deleted dept. Wrap the checks and the delete in a single `@Transactional` block (and/or lock the dept row) so the precondition and the deletion are atomic.

This method has no caller anywhere in the repository (`softDelete` is only referenced by its own declaration; SysOrgController/compat layer has been removed), so the claim in the Javadoc that it is used by the `/api/org` compat layer is stale — it is effectively dead code that should be deleted or, if it is really meant to stay, must at least perform the same permission-cache invalidation as `update()` (soft-deleting a dept changes the hierarchy derived values cached for users of that dept).

Logic mismatch with `scopeFilter`: the list returned by `scopeFilter` is only guaranteed to contain the user's dept chain, and its topmost element may be a node whose `parentId` is NOT 0 (e.g. the group filter prunes a cross-group parent, which is exactly the case the N-06 hardening in `scopeFilter` is meant to survive). `buildTree(all, 0L)` only keeps nodes whose `parentId == 0`, so such a chain is silently dropped and the whole subtree — including the user's own department — disappears from the returned tree (empty tree). Anchor the tree at the actual roots of the filtered list instead of hard-coding 0L, e.g. build a set of ids present in `all` and treat every node whose parentId is absent from that set as a root.

On a large user table this is a full-table UPDATE plus one undo/redo record per row, executed synchronously in the request thread, just for a cache-self-healing fallback. Consider limiting to affected users, using a single shared/global permission version key instead of per-row counters, or making the bump asynchronous.

content: Check-then-act race: two concurrent `create` calls with the same `code` can both see `count == 0` and pass the validation. The DB has `UNIQUE KEY uk_code` on `sys_permission_rule.code`, so the second insert will throw `DuplicateKeyException` (HTTP 500) rather than the intended `BusinessException("规则编码已存在")`. Suggest relying on the unique constraint and translating the violation, e.g. wrap `ruleMapper.insert(rule)` in a try/catch for `org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException` and rethrow as `BusinessException` (the pre-check can stay as a fast path).

`update` is missing the two guards that `create` performs:
1) No existence check — if `id` does not exist (or is null, e.g. a malformed body), `updateById` silently affects 0 rows and the method still returns success while pointlessly wiping the permission cache and bumping every user's `perm_version`.
2) No uniqueness check on `code` — the controller sets id from the path but lets the body carry any `code`, so renaming a rule to an already used code will hit the DB `uk_code` unique index and surface as an unhandled `DuplicateKeyException` (HTTP 500) instead of the friendly `BusinessException("规则编码已存在")` used in `create`.
Also, since the whole entity comes straight from `@RequestBody`, null required fields (name/code/targetEntity/ruleType) are not validated and will fail at the DB NOT NULL constraint.
`getById` is never referenced anywhere: `SysPermissionRuleController` only exposes list/create/update/delete. It is effectively dead code — either wire it to a detail endpoint or remove it.

This runs on every rule create/update/delete and updates the entire `sys_user` table (no WHERE clause), so with a large user table each low-frequency admin action becomes a full-table write (row locks, binlog volume, replication lag). It also deliberately invalidates the permission cache of every user, forcing a full permission-context rebuild on their next request. Note the migrations use `WHERE deleted = 0` for the same statement, so the filter is at least inconsistent here. Suggest adding `WHERE deleted = 0` and, because the identical method is duplicated in `SysDeptService`, `SysRoleService` and `RolePermScopeService`, extracting it into a single shared component that encapsulates the cache eviction + version bump.

content: `countByModule` issues 6 separate `selectCount` statements (1 for "全部" + 5 in this loop). Worse, every `buildBase()` call re-runs `scopeResolver.resolveModuleUsersWithinGroup(...)`, which itself performs permission evaluation and a `GroupScopeUtil.userIdsInGroup(jdbcTemplate, ...)` SQL query — so a single HTTP request to `/api/system/logs/counts` may trigger up to ~12 DB round trips for identical permission data, and the "全部" count is just the sum the DB should compute. Suggest resolving the visible-scope wrapper once and issuing a single `GROUP BY module` aggregate (e.g. `selectMaps` with `.select(SysLog::getModule)` + `groupBy`), then deriving both the per-module map and the total in memory.

`size` comes straight from the request (`@RequestParam(defaultValue = "15")`) and is not clamped here, and no `maxLimit` is configured on `PaginationInnerInterceptor` (MybatisPlusConfig). A caller can therefore pass an arbitrarily large `size` (e.g. `size=1000000`) and force loading/returning the whole `sys_log` table in one request. Clamp the page parameters in the service (e.g. `size = Math.min(Math.max(size, 1), 200)`).

This branch is a fail-open no-op: if a non-admin ever reaches it, no `userId` predicate is added and the query returns the operation logs of the entire platform (exactly the ACL-P1-001 class of bug this code was meant to fix). The comment asserts the invariant is guaranteed by `resolveModuleUsersWithinGroup` (currently true, since that method only returns `null` for users holding the admin role), but the correctness of this security filter then depends silently on a remote method's contract — one refactor of the resolver and audit logs leak platform-wide. Make it fail-closed by default, e.g. treat `null` the same as an empty set (`w.eq(SysLog::getUserId, Long.MIN_VALUE)`) or throw an `IllegalStateException`.

`LocalDate.parse` throws `DateTimeParseException` for any non-`yyyy-MM-dd` value, which is not caught anywhere in this layer and will surface as a 500 error for a simple bad query parameter. There is also no check that `startDate <= endDate` (a reversed range silently returns an empty page). Consider validating the parameters first (parse once, return an empty result or a `Result.error` for malformed/reversed ranges) instead of propagating the runtime exception.

循环内逐次调用 `deptMapper.selectDescendantIds(orgId)`，每次都是一条独立 SQL（N+1）。组织管理员管辖多个组织、且目标部门不在可见列表时，会放大成 N 条递归查询。建议先一次性收集 `getCurrentManagedOrgIds()`，再用一条带 `IN` 的递归/SQL 查询批量取回所有后代部门 ID，最后在内存中判断 `contains(targetDeptId)`。
`deptIds` 来源于前端查询参数，`Long::parseLong` 对非法片段（如 `deptIds=1,abc` 或 `1,` 之外的脏值）会抛出未捕获的 `NumberFormatException`，最终以 500 形式返回而非友好提示。建议过滤非数字片段（或捕获异常后返回空结果/参数错误），保证接口健壮性。

审计事件在参数校验与 `userMapper.insert(user)` **之前**记录，此时 `user.getId()` 恒为 null（新用户主键由插入后才生成），且 `username` 可能为空。结果：审计流水丢失目标用户 ID（无法与后续用户记录关联），同时所有因校验失败而被拒绝的创建请求也会写入一条“user_create”成功语义的审计记录，污染审计轨迹。建议把审计调用移到校验通过、`userMapper.insert(user)` 之后，并传入 `user.getId()`。

此处为不可达的死代码：方法开头已有 `if (!StringUtils.hasText(user.getDataScopeOverride())) throw new BusinessException("数据范围不能为空");`，因此执行到这里时 `hasText(...)` 必然为 true，该分支永远不会进入，`setDataScopeOverride(null)` 也永远不会生效。建议直接删除该分支（或若确实允许“空=跟随角色”，则应把开头的必填校验一并去掉，二者取其一，避免语义矛盾）。

破坏性操作 `purgeByUser` 被放在“用户存在性校验”和“非 admin 操作者禁止删除 admin 账号”这两道授权校验之前执行。语义上属于先做后判（check-after-act）：对不存在的 userId 或未授权的调用者也会先触发草稿清理，仅依赖外层 `@Transactional` 回滚兜底（若未来该方法的事务传播方式或调用链变化，将造成无授权数据删除）。建议将 `purgeByUser` 移到 `user == null` 与 `hasAdminRole` 校验通过之后、正式删除流程之中。

循环内逐条查库（N+1）：对每个选中菜单都要 `selectById(cur)` 查自身、再 `selectById(parentId)` 查父节点，向下还有对 `expanded` 每个元素的一次 `selectById` 权限校验，一次保存可能产生数十次单行查询。建议一次性把涉及的菜单（含祖先链）批量查出并缓存到 `Map<Long, SysMenu>`（如 `menuMapper.selectBatchIds`），后续在内存中遍历父链，避免 N+1。

审计记录的目标角色 ID 恒为 null：此处 `role` 尚未 `insert`，自增主键还没回填，`permissionChange("role_create", role.getId(), ...)` 落库的 detail 永远是 `roleId=null`，无法定位新建角色。另外由于 `create` 带 `@Transactional`，而 `SecurityAuditService.persist` 是普通 `insert`（同事务、非 REQUIRES_NEW），一旦后续校验抛 `BusinessException` 回滚，这条“先写”的审计也会被一并回滚，提前记审计并无收益。建议把审计调用移到 `roleMapper.insert(role)` 之后（或改用独立事务写入），使审计既带真实角色 ID 又不随业务回滚丢失。

content: 部分更新会静默清空 custom 数据范围配置：`saveRoleOrgs` 第一步就执行 `roleOrgMapper.deleteByRoleId(role.getId())`，而此处只要 `dataScope != null` 就调用它。若调用方只传 `dataScope="custom"` 而未带 `orgIds`（`orgIds == null`），已有 role_org 关联会被全部删除且不再回填，角色的自定义数据范围直接变为空。建议仅在 `orgIds` 显式提供、或 dataScope 明确切换到非 custom（需要清空）时才执行保存。
本方法修改角色的 custom 数据范围（并覆盖既有 role_org 配置），属于权限变更，但缺少 `securityAudit.permissionChange(...)` 审计调用，而同类的 create/update/delete 均有记录，导致“谁能看多少数据”的变更在审计日志中出现盲区。建议在保存前补一条审计事件（如 `role_update_orgs`）。
